thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: prod inference p95 in us-west1 > 700ms for the last 6m. Alerts triggered: latency_p95_high, token_queue_depth_up. Runbook: follow paging checklist.
ana: on it. I'm looking at routing + queue metrics now.
ana: quick check — no obvious infra OOMs or GPU memory errors in the last 10m. CPU on control plane ok.
tom: I see a surge from a noisy tenant sending long-gen requests (avg seq len 1024). Queue depth up on pool gw-uw1.
lina: can we reroute new requests to standby pool in us-west2 while we mitigate? Fallback to q4_0 quantized variant for non-SLAs to reduce token time.
mike: proposing immediate mitigations: 1) enable adaptive batching = aggressive. 2) spin up 4 extra workers in uw1 (burst capacity). 3) update routing policy to prefer uw2 for new sessions. 4) model-fallback to q4 for non-enterprise customers.
mike: running scale command now:
```bash
redwoodctl scale pool gw-uw1 --add 4 --timeout 300
redwoodctl set-routing-policy prod --region-preference uw2 --weight 0.6
```
ana: doing canary routing change for 10% of traffic -> uw2, will monitor p95.
jack: heads-up — customers with reserved capacity shouldn't be moved. We'll exclude those prefixes by tag `reserved:true`.
lina: config to enable model fallback (non-enterprise):
```json
{"route_filter": "customer.tags.reserved != true", "fallback_model": "rw-q4_0-opt:2026-02", "max_seq_len": 8192}
```
mike: applied batch policy and started additional workers. Initial signal: queue depth down 22%, p95 dropping to ~480ms in 2m after change.
ana: updating status page draft — keeping it factual and minimal.
cs-bot: STATUSPAGE: Incident created (INC-1765432100). Current impact: Elevated p95 latency in us-west1 affecting text-generation endpoints for some users. Updates will follow.
jack: here's a short customer notification draft for impacted customers (we'll only send to customers with >1% error/latency hit):
"""
Subject: Brief service note — temporary latency increase in us-west region

Hi —

We're investigating an elevated latency affecting text generation in the us-west region. We've initiated mitigations (traffic routing and capacity scaling) and expect visible improvement within ~30 minutes. If you see sustained impact or have reserved capacity concerns, reply and we'll prioritize.

Apologies for the disruption — Redwood Inference team
"""
ana: good. I'll post that to the status page after Mike confirms p95 under 500ms for 5m.
tom: handing overnight on-call to @ana -> @mike will be primary owner for the mitigations; I'll stay nearby for escalation.
mike: will monitor dashboards and the token queue. If p95 flattens under 450ms for 5 cycles, we'll close incident and publish full postmortem template.
lina: root-cause hypothesis: burst of long-seq requests + model selection (non-quantized) causing large KV cache churn + batching inefficiency. We'll run a postmortem to verify and consider stronger short-seq isolation limits and automatic fallback heuristics.
ana: timeline note for postmortem: include exact tenant id pattern, sequence length distribution, routing policy timeline, and cost impact of scale.
ana: ETA for expected recovery: 20-30 minutes from now. Will update in 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mike: p95 at 430ms now, token queue stable. I'm preparing the status update:
```
We are continuing to see elevated p95 latency in the us-west region. Mitigations (routing to uw2, scale up, and fallback to q4 for eligible traffic) have reduced latency. We expect continued improvements; next update in 15 minutes.
```
ana: posting status update now.
cs-bot: STATUSPAGE: Update posted to INC-1765432100.
ana: handoff complete — @mike monitoring. Please escalate to eng-sre if we regress. :thumbsup:
